_doc: Remote NVMe tuning of the lazy-checkpoint interval (cardinality cliff). Runs on the 6-lane c4d-standard-64-lssd multilane cluster (one physical NVMe per WAL shard, MULTILANE=1 SERVER_LOCAL_SSD_BLOCK=1 SPOT_SERVER=1). All arms use --wal-shards 6 + --wal-checkpoint-syncfs on; the ONLY variable is --wal-checkpoint-interval-ms. ref-syncfs-3s is the reference (PR #4697 cadence on the SAME binary); 30s/60s/120s sweep the amortization knob. Local kind showed monotonic gains 3s->30s->60s at 50k with 60s still climbing, so this pushes to 120s to find the knee. Success = higher throughput at 100k as the interval grows; the winning value + the WAL_CKPT fsync cadence/cost (--wal-stats 3) sets the production default. Watch retained-WAL growth (larger interval = larger WAL + longer crash-replay) as the ceiling.
